title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Persian: A Preliminary Study Focusing on ChatGPT
extended_summary:
This paper benchmarks large language models for Persian across a set of NLP tasks, asking how GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, and OpenChat-3.5 perform on classic, reasoning, and knowledge-based language tasks in a low-resource language setting. The authors are motivated by the lack of comprehensive Persian evaluation and by the question of whether instruction prompting, few-shot examples, and translation into English improve model performance.

The evaluated tasks include sentiment analysis, emotion recognition, named entity recognition, reading comprehension, machine translation, textual entailment, multiple-choice QA, elementary-school math questions, and mathematical problems. The study compares LLMs against task-specific fine-tuned SOTA models on subsets of 200 examples for several tasks, and also tests prompt language (Persian vs English), zero/one/three-shot settings, and translated examples. The educationally relevant portions are the newly created elementary school and 7th/10th grade math question benchmarks, but these are used as language/reasoning benchmarks rather than an instructional intervention study.

Overall, GPT-4 performs best among the tested LLMs and often improves with more shots, while GPT-3.5 is less consistent and sometimes degrades with additional demonstrations. In classic tasks, task-specific fine-tuned models remain stronger for NER, emotion recognition, and reading comprehension; in some reasoning tasks, GPT-4 approaches or exceeds SOTA. Translating prompts/examples into English generally improves GPT-3.5, suggesting strong language sensitivity. This paper does not evaluate K-12 reading or literacy instruction interventions, nor does it provide comparative evidence on generative AI used in classrooms.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI generative large language model chatbot based on GPT-family models used for instruction-following, question answering, translation, and text generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 and GPT-4 on Persian NLP benchmarks, including reading comprehension, with comparisons against task-specific SOTA models and across Persian vs. English prompts and few-shot settings.

findings.finding_summary: On the reading comprehension task (ParsiNLU), ChatGPT models scored below the task-specific SOTA model. GPT-3.5 achieved F1=.535/.643/.642 in Persian prompts (0/1/3-shot) and .588/.644/.644 in English prompts; GPT-4 achieved .564/.646/.659 in Persian and .603/.673/.687 in English, compared with SOTA F1=.691. The paper reports that one-shot results improved over zero-shot by large margins, but even the best ChatGPT result remained below SOTA.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical benchmark study, but not a randomized or quasi-experimental K-12 literacy intervention study. It provides direct comparative evidence on a reading comprehension benchmark, yet the work is primarily NLP evaluation rather than educational impact evaluation.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational effect size is reported, and the paper does not evaluate classroom literacy outcomes or instructional impact. The closest relevant result is a benchmark F1 comparison showing ChatGPT below SOTA on reading comprehension.
